title: 12-Lead ECG
author: K. Aldana, MD
summary: Sinus tachycardia 124, PR 138 ms, QRS 84 ms, QT/QTc 296/426 ms. Peaked, narrow, symmetric T waves V2-V4; hyperkalemia suspected (BMP pending).
body:
**Measurements**
Ventricular rate 124 bpm. PR 138 ms. QRS 84 ms. QT/QTc 296/426 ms (Bazett: RR 60/124 = 0.484 s; square root 0.696; 0.296 / 0.696 = 0.426).

**Interpretation**
Sinus tachycardia. Tall, narrow, symmetric, peaked T waves in V2 to V4. P waves present; PR and QRS normal (no signs of severe hyperkalemia). No ST changes. No arrhythmia.

**Context**
Suspected DKA in a 22-year-old with no known diabetes; POC glucose 548. Peaked T waves suggest a high potassium: acidosis and no insulin move potassium out of the cells. BMP pending. Potassium must be known before insulin starts.
impression: Sinus tachycardia 124 with peaked T waves V2-V4, suggesting hyperkalemia. QTc 426 ms. BMP pending.
